title: Maximum flow: Edmonds-Karp vs push-relabel vs almost-linear time
problem_statement: Given a directed graph with integer edge capacities, a source s and a sink t, compute the value of a maximum s-t flow.

input.parameter: n vertices, m edges (capacities polynomially bounded integers for the almost-linear bound).
input.size_measure: Theta(m log U) bits, U = largest capacity.

algorithms.name: Edmonds-Karp
algorithms.pseudocode: while a BFS augmenting path exists in the residual graph: push the bottleneck along it

algorithms.name: push-relabel (Goldberg-Tarjan)
algorithms.idea: Maintain a preflow and vertex heights; push excess downhill, relabel when stuck.
algorithms.time_complexity: O(n m log(n^2 / m)) with dynamic trees

algorithms.name: almost-linear-time max flow (Chen et al.)
algorithms.idea: Interior-point method on min-cost flow, each step solved by a dynamic data structure for approximate min-ratio cycles.
algorithms.pseudocode: Chen, Kyng, Liu, Peng, Probst Gutenberg, Sachdeva 2022
algorithms.correctness: Chen et al. 2022 (randomized; a deterministic version followed in later work).

relationship: All polynomial; O(n m^2) -> O(n m log(n^2/m)) -> m^(1+o(1)).

sources.authors: Ford, L. R.; Fulkerson, D. R.
sources.title: Maximal flow through a network
Theoretical improvements in algorithmic efficiency for network flow problems

sources.authors: Goldberg, A. V.; Tarjan, R. E.
sources.title: A new approach to the maximum-flow problem

sources.authors: Chen, L.; Kyng, R.; Liu, Y. P.; Peng, R.; Probst Gutenberg, M.; Sachdeva, S.
sources.title: Maximum Flow and Minimum-Cost Flow in Almost-Linear Time

verification.method: Cited from the literature; not independently implemented.

caveats: The almost-linear algorithm is far from practical; its m^(o(1)) factor hides large terms. The m^(1+o(1)) bound assumes polynomially bounded integer capacities.
notes: Not implemented here; Edmonds-Karp vs Dinic is a separate V1 entry (pairs/max-flow-edmonds-karp-vs-dinic). The almost-linear algorithm is cited only.
